name: Structure of Atom
overview: The Pauli Exclusion Principle Helium atom has two electrons. Hund’s rule: The orbitals of equal energy (degenerate) are occupied with one electron each before pairing of electrons starts. Following orbital diagram shows the electron configuration of nitrogen atom.

vsaq.question: Complete the key idea: The Pauli Exclusion Principle Helium atom has two _____.
vsaq.answer: The Pauli Exclusion Principle Helium atom has two electrons.

vsaq.question: Complete the key idea: Following orbital diagram shows the _____ configuration of nitrogen atom.
vsaq.answer: Following orbital diagram shows the electron configuration of nitrogen atom.

vsaq.question: Complete the key idea: Aufbau principle: The lowest-energy _____ are filled first.
vsaq.answer: Aufbau principle: The lowest-energy orbitals are filled first.

vsaq.question: Complete the key idea: _____ waves can have a wide variety of wavelengths.
vsaq.answer: Electromagnetic waves can have a wide variety of wavelengths.

vsaq.question: Complete the key idea: As the frequency increases, the _____ becomes smaller.
vsaq.answer: As the frequency increases, the wavelength becomes smaller.

vsaq.question: Complete the key idea: Those are the Pauli Exclusion _____, Aufbau principle and Hund’s Rule.
vsaq.answer: Those are the Pauli Exclusion Principle, Aufbau principle and Hund’s Rule.

vsaq.question: Complete the key idea: How many sub shells are present in a principal _____ level? e.
vsaq.answer: How many sub shells are present in a principal energy level? e.

vsaq.question: Complete the key idea: The range of _____ covering red colour to violet colour is called the visible spectrum.
vsaq.answer: The range of wavelengths covering red colour to violet colour is called the visible spectrum.

vsaq.question: Complete the key idea: The magnetic _____ number (ml) has integer values between -l and l, including zero.
vsaq.answer: The magnetic quantum number (ml) has integer values between -l and l, including zero.

vsaq.question: Complete the key idea: Each value of ‘l’ is related to the shape of a particular sub-shell in the space around the _____.
vsaq.answer: Each value of ‘l’ is related to the shape of a particular sub-shell in the space around the nucleus.

saq.question: Explain wavelength and frequency with reference to Structure of Atom.
saq.answer: The wavelength (λ) of the wave is the distance from one wave peak to the next. The frequency (υ) of a wave is simply the number of wave peaks that pass by a given point per unit time, expressed in units of reciprocal

saq.question: Explain characterized and wavelengths with reference to Structure of Atom.
saq.answer: Each colour in a rainbow is characterized by a specified wavelength from red (higher wavelength) to violet (shorter wavelength). These colours (wavelengths), that the human naked eye is sensitive to, are called visible

saq.question: Explain electromagnetic and wavelengths with reference to Structure of Atom.
saq.answer: The electromagnetic spectrum consists of a continuous range of wavelengths of gamma rays at the shorter wavelength to radio waves at the longer wavelength. But our eyes are sensitive only to visible light.

saq.question: Explain energies and electron with reference to Structure of Atom.
saq.answer: The energies of an electron in an atom can have only certain values E1, E2, E3 ……; that is, the energy is quantized. The states corresponding to these energies are called stationary states and the possible values of the energy are called energy levels.
